messages:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered -> SEV: P1 | symptom: GPU request queue growth in eu-west-3 (aws) exceeding alert threshold. Auto-scaler alerts + elevated enqueue rate. @oncall please take. :rotating_light:
Maria G: I'm on it — seeing queue jump from ~120 to 900 over 6m, 90th percentile latency for requests now 48s. Autoscaler shows repeated provision attempts stuck 'PROVISIONING' and then falling back with errors.
Samir P: grabbing provider console. early note: a bunch of instances are in PROVISIONING state with API errors. Looks like EC2 is returning a 429 + "CapacityAllocationTimeout" for spot/non-spot mixes.
Maria G: logs snippet from autoscaler:
```
2026-02-18T12:07:12Z autoscaler INFO request=scale_up attempt=17 state=PROVISIONING err="ResourceAllocationError: CapacityAllocationTimeout (retryable)"
2026-02-18T12:07:18Z autoscaler WARN backlog=842 inflight=32
```
Samir P: also seeing a flurry of API rate limit responses to DescribeCapacityPools — might be cloud-side throttling. Not a plain quota denial, looks like allocation contention in the region.
Jonathan K: impact calc — ingestion queue has 6k tokens waiting, estimate 25-30% of hosted customers using GPU routes in eu-west-3 experiencing >2x latency. No full 503 flood yet but timeouts start at 60s.
Lee H: can we temporarily route low-priority traffic to eu-west-1? We have spare capacity there. That's a config change in the router; need to update routing policy and kick a soft rollback plan.
Anya R: heads-up: two enterprise customers (bigshop-inc, healthstack) reported slower responses on their dashboards. Support already opened tickets.
Maria G: Actions I'm initiating now: 1) pause all non-critical batch jobs across eu-west-3 pools, 2) mark low-priority routes as 'degraded' so router won't pick GPUs for them, 3) attempt parallel provisioning in eu-west-1 as Lee suggested.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: GPU-region-provisioning -> step 3: escalate to cloud support if allocation timeout > 10 minutes; step 5: consider cross-region reroute. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-provisioning
Samir P: manual check: calling AWS API returned this for a sample allocate call:
```
{"Error": {"Code": "CapacityAllocationTimeout", "Message": "Unable to allocate capacity in requested AZ within timeout"}}
```
Samir P: I've opened a support case with AWS — case #2026-83712. Also requested rate-limit lift for our describe/capacity APIs in the region. ETA from support unknown.
Jonathan K: mitigation proposal: (A) re-route ~40% of traffic to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 where we have spare pools, (B) scale down non-essential dev pools in eu-west-3 (can reclaim ~60 GPUs), (C) enable preemptible-only fallback for low-priority jobs (will reduce cost but buys headroom).
Maria G: doing B now: draining dev and internal test pools in eu-west-3 — kicking the drain job.
Lee H: I'll take care of A. Pushed a controlled routing override to divert selected customer prefixes to eu-west-1. Watch for cross-region latency increases.
Anya R: coordinating comms: posting incident banner to status page and flagging the two affected enterprise customers. Drafting message for support to use in tickets.
Maria G: started enabling preemptible-only fallback for non-urgent routes. NOT enabling for enterprise-dedicated customers.
ops-runbook-bot: Note: step 7 completed -> temporary routing override applied.
Samir P: After draining dev pools, we reclaimed ~48 GPUs. Autoscaler successfully provisioned 12 instances in eu-west-3 afterwards but allocation is still slow — backlog decreased from 900 -> 420 in 9m.
Jonathan K: early customer impact summary: roughly 18% of requests in the region saw latency >30s, 3% returned timeouts/503. Critical SLAs for enterprise customers preserved by Dedicated fallbacks.
Maria G: starting to compile timeline for handoff. Next oncall is Jonathan K at 13:00 UTC — handing off with list of open actions and pending cloud ticket.
Samir P: AWS support replied: "We see transient inventory pressure in eu-west-3 AZ 'c' due to large marketplace demands; we're throttling allocation to protect platform stability. Suggesting cross-AZ allocation or queuing allocations." Ticket updated: AWS-2026-83712 -> engineers investigating.
Jonathan K: taking handoff. Summary for next oncall: root cause suspected: sudden regional capacity pressure + cloud-side allocation throttling causing autoscaler provisioning to stall -> request queue growth. Current mitigation status: routing override live, dev pools drained, preemptible fallback enabled for low-priority, ~60 GPUs reclaimed, backlog halved but not cleared. Open items: 1) follow AWS ticket until allocation restored, 2) monitor queue until <100, 3) consider adjusting autoscaler provisioning window to be more aggressive (needs follow-up change), 4) draft post-incident customer notes.
Maria G: assigning postmortem owner -> Jonathan K. He'll own timeline + remediation proposals (autoscaler backoff tuning, cross-region warm-pool strategy).
Anya R: customer comms plan: initial banner on status page, targeted emails to affected enterprise contacts with mitigation details and ETA estimate (TBD).
Jonathan K: noted. I'll leave a checklist for the next shift. If allocation doesn't recover in 45m, we'll expand cross-region failover and consider provisioning additional warm pools in eu-west-1 to absorb steady-state traffic.
Maria G: thanks team. Handoff complete. Closing live pagers for this shift — will monitor and reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
